purpose: paired tests behind F12's proxy-agreement and selectivity claims
headline: criterion alignment removes proxy-negative admits at ~2x the rate of proxy-positive admits (Fisher p<0.001), but overall agreement with the proxy does not improve (McNemar p~0.5). It is a precision/recall tradeoff.
proxy_caveat: topic_label_v2 is the authors' arXiv primary-category declaration, not a definitive judgement of aboutness

A_proxy_agreement_paired.test: McNemar exact, per-row decision vs proxy label
A_proxy_agreement_paired.verdict: no significant change in overall agreement with the proxy

B_selectivity_of_removal.test: Fisher exact, [removed,kept] x [was FP, was TP]
B_selectivity_of_removal.verdict: proxy-negative admits are removed at a higher rate

C_proxy_relative_ledger.note: More proxy-positive rows were removed than proxy-negative rows; proxy precision rose because the rate of proxy-negative removal was higher, not because these rows were adjudicated errors.
